rows.27:ad14:
I was saved.
I didn't know what that thing just now was, but at least it hadn't been after {f:me|me}.
The moment my shoulders slumped in relief, I could suddenly move again.
I tried moving both hands.
Feeling had come back to my tongue, too, which had been like stiff rubber.
{f:I|I} muttered without thinking.
"What {f:the hell was that|was that}...?"
I shook my head lightly and stood up.
Then, for no particular reason, I looked behind me.{p}
rows.27:b190:
My mind went blank, and I felt so sleepy I could hardly stand it.
Maybe I should just fall asleep like this.
{f:I|I} curled up on the floor and hugged my knees.
I heard someone's voice.
Sleep... sleep...
That body of yours... I'll be taking it...
...Whose voice was that?
Had {f:I|I} {f:fallen|fallen} into the trap of some demon that had made its nest in this school?
...But I didn't care anymore{f:|}.
{f:I|I} was sleepy{f:|}.
I'd just go to sleep like this{f:|}...... forever.
In the moment I drifted off, I felt a wicked will inside my body.
But what that meant...{p}{f:I|I} no longer had the strength even to think about it.{p}
rows.27:b720:
Why, you ask...
That time, there were six students kept behind.
Four boys and two girls.
But there were seven students who'd gotten failing grades.
And yet the last one never showed up.
...A lot like us today, isn't it?{p}
rows.27:c044:
Before I knew it, Hosoda was standing there.
"No, um... I just thought the stains moved a second ago."
As I said it, a sudden wave of embarrassment welled up in me.
Stains, moving?
It was like a frightened child seeing a curtain sway and deciding it was a ghost{f:|}.
{f:I'd seen things only because I was so scared|Maybe I'd seen things only because I was so scared}.
"...It's nothing."
"Is that so?
Then let's go back."{p}
rows.27:c718:
There was a school bag lying in the hallway.
Someone picked it up and said,
"This is his bag."
...That's what they said.
That's right, it was the seventh one's bag.
Had he overheard them badmouthing him?
The six looked at each other.
They must have thought they were in trouble.{p}
rows.27:cacc:
The girls screamed too.
But one of them, keeping a cool head, pointed at it.
"Isn't that fake?"
...That's what they said.
Now that they looked, there wasn't a single drop of blood on the cut end.
The color was kind of whitish, too.
"It's him!"{p}
rows.27:ce20:
It was a leg, from the knee down.
They all snickered.
If he meant to be hiding, they thought, it was a ridiculously stupid way to go about it.
"Come on, cut it out.
We all know it's you..."
The one saying that peeked into the restroom and broke off mid-sentence.{p}
rows.27:d560:
All kinds of weird rumors spread, too: that strange groans could be heard from the girls' restroom on the third floor of the old school building, or that someone had seen the missing students there.
So people started saying it was Hanako-san's curse.
That Hanako-san had taken the six of them away.
Whether those six wandered into another world, or whether it really was Hanako-san's curse, nobody knows.{p}
rows.27:d6cc:
But the one I feel sorry for is the seventh one.
Unlike the other six, nobody knew he'd been in the old school building, so he was treated differently.
He was a bit of a delinquent, so people even suspected he'd run away from home.
Talk about adding insult to injury.
But... why would he come back so late like that?
If he was skipping the make-up class, he could've just gone straight home.
...Maybe he'd been there from the very beginning.
And Hanako-san caught him.
Right above the heads of everyone taking the make-up class, Hanako-san may have been hacking him to pieces...
...And that's the end of the story about the old school building.
Of course, nobody actually saw them being killed, so it isn't very credible, is it?{p}
rows.27:e094:
On the back of the clock, the side opposite the face, black clumps {f:were|were} clinging in a thick layer.
And they were squirming.{p}
rows.27:e200:
"What's the matter, {a}{f:|}?
And here I've got a really good scary story ready just for you."
As he spoke, the black things were crawling up to his chest.
They were bugs{f:|}.
Tiny bugs like flying ants, thousands upon thousands of them, swarming together{f:|}.
"You're a strange one."
As Hosoda said that, black winged bugs spilled out of his mouth in clumps.
{f:I|I} couldn't believe my eyes.
But the bugs kept spilling from the mouth and nostrils of a puzzled-looking Hosoda.
With a rip, a split opened in his cheek.
And bugs came gushing out of that split, too.
By now, Hosoda's whole body was black, buried in crawling bugs.
And still, Hosoda kept on talking.{p}
